Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
639 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Temperatures were running warmer than forecast thanks to thick cloud 
cover so blended in some warmer guidance through the morning hours. 

Latest guidance showed the main rain shield coming in a bit slower 
so trimmed PoPs back a bit through the morning hours. 

Slower PoPs combined with warmer morning temps should keep any 
wintry precip at bay this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the area
today and Thanksgiving Day. There is potential for frequent wind
gusts strong enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures
such as tents and holiday decorations, and produce isolated power
outages. Widespread rainfall is expected with locally heavy rain
possible, however the overall flood risk appears low.
2. Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue through
Friday with light wintry precipitation possible near the Tennessee
border. Warmer for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the 
area today and Thanksgiving Day. There is potential for frequent 
wind gusts strong enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures 
such as tents and holiday decorations, and produce isolated power 
outages. Widespread rainfall is expected with locally heavy rain 
possible, however the overall flood risk appears low.

Sprawling sfc high pressure centered to our north continues to  
produce gusty NE winds and relatively dry dewpts across our area. 
As the morning progresses, the high is expected to strengthen a bit 
more under confluent upper flow. This will result in a classical CAD 
set-up that will impact much of the East Coast including our CWA, 
thru at least Thursday morning. Precipitation chances increase from 
south to north thru the day today, but it's still looking like 
precip doesn't begin until temperatures warm above freezing, and/or 
cloud cover keeps temps above freezing altogether. Temperatures 
remain steady or even warm later tonight and into Thursday as wedge 
erosion begins. Thus, no wintry precip appears possible during this 
period. 

Consensus is strengthening for a robust sfc low to develop over the
east coast of Florida later today and track northward. Moist ELY flow
over the damming sfc high results in widespread precip for our CWA by
this evening, continuing overnight before generally tapering off 
from SW to NE during Thanksgiving Day. Overall, forecast rainfall 
amounts remain similar to previous fcsts but they have trended a bit 
higher over most of our NC Piedmont and foothill zones. We now have 
1 to 2" storm total amounts fcst across a good portion of those 
areas. Still, few global model ensemble members develop enough QPF 
for much of a flood risk. It is possible that a narrow, 
frontogenetically-forced band of heavy rain could develop west of 
the low track, which models may not resolve well. Nonetheless, the 
flash flood threat still appears low and likely secondary to the 
threat posed by strong/gusty winds. WPC maintains a Marginal Risk 
for most of our fcst area on the Day 1 Excessive Rainfall Outlook. 

As for the winds, we are still expecting anomalously strong easterly 
925 to 850mb winds associated with the LLJ, with winds of 45 to 50 kt 
possible a couple thousand feet above ground over the Piedmont. Given 
the strength of the wedge and the associated inversion, we still expect 
only shallow mixing and thus these higher gusts will likely be limited 
over the Piedmont. Nonetheless, there is good support among the 
latest model guidance for frequent 30 to 45 mph gusts this afternoon 
thru Thursday morning. Peak winds for the event will likely be 
closer to 45 mph for most locations with higher gusts expected at 
the higher elevations (above 3500 ft). After consultation with our 
neighboring fcst offices, we decided to expand the Wind Advisory to 
include our entire CWA. The valid time remains the same as the 
initial Advisory, noon today until 10 AM Thursday. This was largely 
done because of the potential for significant impacts across our 
area. A few power outages could result and gusts will be capable of 
blowing over holiday decorations, tents, portable canopies, etc, 
many of which are only rated for 25 mph gusts. Be prepared for wind 
gusts to turn over outdoor cooking appliances; have a fire 
extinguisher handy.


Key message 2: Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue
through Friday with light wintry precipitation possible near the 
Tennessee border. Warmer for the weekend.

A noticeable lull in wind speed appears likely Thursday morning as 
low pressure pulls away to the north and before cold-air advection 
on its back side induces stronger mixing. Gusty winds are expected 
to return Thursday afternoon and continue thru Friday. We cannot 
completely rule out Advisory-level gusts over the higher mountain 
elevations, but the threat still appears lower compared to today
thru Thursday morning. Temperatures are expected to rebound to within 
a few degrees of normal for Thursday afternoon, but trend colder again 
Thursday night. Light NW-flow precipitation Thurs night may change to 
a wintry mix, if not snow or rime ice. It's looking like there should 
be sufficient moisture to maintain at least a solid-chance PoP along 
portions of the NC/TN border thru the day Friday. Any accumulations 
should be minimal. 

Temperatures trend warmer over the weekend. More of the latest long-
range guidance now has a fast-moving cold front push thru our area
late Sunday into early Monday with some amount of precip associated
with the fropa. If this scenario pans out, temperatures should be 
warm enough that only rain is possible.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Gusty winds have already developed across 
the terminals with the exception of KAVL. Gusts should develop by 
late morning or late afternoon at KAVL. Gusty winds will linger 
across the terminals through the end of the 12Z TAF period. Wind 
gusts will range from 20-30 kts through the morning hours, 
increasing to 25-35 kts this afternoon into tonight. OVC through the 
period with RA and restrictions gradually spreading over the 
terminals through late afternoon. Maintained PROB30s for the onset 
of RA and restrictions as guidance is still not in great agreement 
regarding the arrival time of rain. Once RA starts, it will linger 
though tonight so have prevailing RA once PROB30s end.Already seeing 
MVFR cigs for as of 1130Z across most of the SC terminals and KCLT. 
The rest of the terminals should see cigs should drop to MVFR this 
morning. Cigs should drop to IFR this afternoon. LIFR cigs may 
develop at KCLT briefly this evening but confidence remains too low 
to mention in the TAF. Vsby restrictions will mostly be MVFR to IFR 
with the RA shield. 

Outlook: Widespread rain, gusty winds and associated restrictions 
will gradually wane Thursday as a strong low pressure system lifts 
away from the terminals. Drier and VFR conditions return Thursday 
night into Saturday but gusty winds will return Thursday afternoon 
and should linger into Friday evening.
